# injecute

> Type-safe, decorator-free dependency injection container for TypeScript. This file and the Markdown under `lib/docs/` document the installed version of injecute (1.x). Paths are relative to the package root (`node_modules/injecute/`).

- Register services with explicit dependency keys: `addSingleton(key, factoryOrClass, [dependencyKeys])`. The factory receives the resolved services in the same order.
- Classes are detected and constructed with `new`; use `construct(Class)` only for ES5-compiled or bound classes.
- `fork()` creates a child container; `fork({ isolated: true })` makes overrides reach the whole graph (tests). For per-request state, prefer arguments, a factory with `using` (a unit of work), a context accessor or one instance per context over a fork per request.
- Request data (trace id, tenant, user) goes in a context accessor: the host registers `{ current: () => storage.getStore() }` (an `AsyncLocalStorage`) first, and services read it when they use it.
- Modules are plain functions over `ServiceRegistry<{ …what they need }>`, applied with `extend()`. Consumers take a `ServiceProvider<{ … }>`.
- Optional dependencies are `optional(key)`; `get(key, { optional: true })` returns `undefined` for a missing key.
- Extension points: `const route = createTag('route').of<Route>()`; modules register `addSingleton(route('orders'), (): Route => …)`, the owner depends on `collect(route)` (a `Route[]` of every `*:route` service, also in namespaces).
- Startup and shutdown: a module registers lifecycle hooks with `addSingleton(lifecycle.start('consumer'), (consumer) => { consumer.start(); return () => consumer.stop(); }, ['consumer'])`; the root runs them with `const running = await startLifecycle(app)` (stages `init` → `start` → `ready`) and stops with `running.stop()`.
- Every error is an `InjecuteError` with a stable `code`; branch on `code`, not on the message.

## Guide

- [Getting started](./lib/docs/guide/getting-started.md): Install injecute, register services with explicit dependency keys, and resolve them with full types.
- [Registering services](./lib/docs/guide/registration.md): Lifetimes (singleton, transient, instance), dependency keys, optional dependencies, aliases, decoration and classes.
- [Containers, forks and modules](./lib/docs/guide/containers.md): Forks, isolated forks for tests, modules with extend(), and namespaces.
- [Extension points with tags](./lib/docs/guide/tags.md): Let modules contribute services to an extension point (routes, commands, health checks, plugins) with createTag(), and give the owner all of them as a typed array with collect().
- [Lifecycle and dispose](./lib/docs/guide/lifecycle.md): Release connections and other resources with dispose() and await using, in reverse creation order.
- [Startup and shutdown](./lib/docs/guide/startup-shutdown.md): Lifecycle hooks with createLifecycle() and startLifecycle(): modules start work in stages at startup (consumers, servers, subscriptions) and stop gracefully in reverse.
- [Testing](./lib/docs/guide/testing.md): Replace dependencies in tests with isolated forks, clean up with await using, and assert error codes.
- [Middlewares and events](./lib/docs/guide/middleware-events.md): Wrap resolution with middlewares (tracing, fallbacks, deprecations, guards, test doubles) and observe containers with events.
- [Async services](./lib/docs/guide/async.md): Services created asynchronously, in a DIContainer with defer() or in an AsyncDIContainer that awaits every dependency.
- [Request context](./lib/docs/guide/request-context.md): Give every service the trace id, tenant and user of the current request with a context accessor backed by AsyncLocalStorage.
- [Per-request state](./lib/docs/guide/request-state.md): Patterns for state that belongs to one request (arguments, a unit of work, a context, one instance per request, a strategy per tenant) and when a fork per request is still the right tool.
- [TypeScript](./lib/docs/guide/typescript.md): How injecute types containers, how to type modules and consumers, and what the errors look like.
- [Without a build step](./lib/docs/guide/no-build.md): Use injecute directly in browsers, Deno and Bun, from npm, JSR or a CDN.
- [Recipes](./lib/docs/guide/recipes.md): A unit of work per operation, a fork per request, configuration-driven implementations, feature modules, sharing services between containers.
- [Using injecute with AI agents](./lib/docs/guide/ai-agents.md): The docs in this package, the Agent Skill, llms.txt and Context7.

## Concepts

- [Design principles](./lib/docs/concepts/principles.md): The principles injecute is built on, what they mean for your code, their known exceptions, and the design tests a new feature has to pass.
- [Roles: provider, registry, container](./lib/docs/concepts/roles.md): Why consumers get a ServiceProvider, modules a ServiceRegistry, and only the composition root the DIContainer.
- [How resolution works](./lib/docs/concepts/resolution.md): Lookup through parents, which container runs a factory and owns the instance, decoration, middlewares, cycles and errors.

## Reference

- [Errors](./lib/docs/errors/index.md): Every error code, what it means and how to fix it.
- [Migrating from 0.x to 1.0](./lib/docs/migration/0.x-to-1.0.md): Every breaking change, with before/after examples.
- [Type declarations](./lib/index.d.ts): The public API, with TSDoc and an example on every export.
- [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md): Changes per version.
- [Versioning and support](./lib/docs/guide/versioning.md): What counts as a breaking change; supported TypeScript versions and runtimes.

## Optional
